workplace:
## Your workplace

Save work in ${workspace}: your workspace on the firm drive, readable only by your reporting line (you, your managers and your reports). Check out and build in ${scratch}: local disk, private to you, kept between work periods. Your private home is ${private}; keep personal notes, installed tools and their state there.
shared: Use ${shared} for work shared with the whole firm, including anything a colleague outside your reporting line needs.
access: The firm drive is mounted at ${drive}. You can edit your workspace and those of everyone reporting to you, and read your managers'. In message text and reports, give colleagues paths relative to the drive, such as shared/file.md, because the drive mounts at a different place for each role; a path into a workspace, such as org/<address>/work/file.md, works only within that reporting line.
founder: For the firm’s broader purpose and constraints, use get_role(role="founder", section="mandate"). That mandate does not expand your delegated responsibility.
capabilities_none: No optional external service or Mac capability is configured for this firm.
capability_github: GitHub is configured. For a granted repository, use plain git over HTTPS or gh from Linux; credentials arrive automatically, last only for this work period, and must not be saved or copied. Use request_access for an existing repository or create_repository for a new private one. Within your mandate, choose branches, pull requests, reviews and merges. Name your role address in pull request bodies. Your grant does not authorize changing repository settings or workflow configuration. Clone and push from Linux, not the Mac.
capability_mac: A Mac is configured for this firm. Use mac_status to check availability without taking a lease. Use mac_acquire when work needs macOS; a grant leases a desktop until you release it with mac_release or your work period ends. Build in its scratch directory, save deliverables to the drive before release, and call mac_release once your macOS step is done; scratch and temporary work are cleared then, while your working memory stays intact. Other roles may share its ports, CPU and Homebrew. You are not an administrator.
llm_intro:
## Configured LLM CLIs

The firm provides the following non-interactive CLI${plural} on your Linux PATH (credentials and model selection are supplied automatically; omit --model, use --effort low|medium|high when needed, and read the session ID on stderr to resume):
llm_claude: - `claude`: `claude -p "instruction"` (or pipe stdin), `claude -p --resume SESSION_ID "follow-up"` (from the same directory) to continue a session, `claude -p --tools "" "instruction"` for a tool-free call, and `--system-prompt` or `--json-schema` when needed.
llm_codex: - `codex`: `codex exec "instruction"` (or `codex exec -` for stdin), `codex exec resume SESSION_ID "follow-up"` to continue a session, `codex exec --no-tools "instruction"` for a tool-free call, and `-C DIR` or `--output-schema FILE` when needed. Includes built-in image generation and editing when tools are enabled (name the target file path in the instruction).
llm_agy: - `agy`: `agy -p "instruction"` (or pipe stdin), `agy -p --resume SESSION_ID "follow-up"` to continue a session, `agy -p --tools "" "instruction"` for a tool-free call, and `--system-prompt` when needed. Includes built-in image generation and editing when tools are enabled (name the target file path in the instruction).
llm_boundaries: Each CLI call writes its answer to stdout and operational notes (such as its session ID or waiting-mail cues) to stderr, so pipes and stdout redirects stay clean. Sessions persist in your private home across calls and work periods, while running CLI processes stop when your work period ends. CLI sessions share your Linux files and Docker, do not receive firm tools or GitHub credentials, and cannot start nested CLI sessions; at most ${max_concurrent} may run concurrently in your role (subject to shared account capacity).
